mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility is recovering first among out-of-home channels, rising 6.8 points from t-1w (-50.4) to t-0w (-43.6). Rebuilt transit volume proxies the return of chained out-of-home routines, and because transit trips bundle discretionary stops, RETAIL_REC follows transit recovery with a short lag.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -51.0 at t-3w to -43.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week while the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Residential-stay surplus is eroding, falling from +14.9 at t-3w to +9.4 at t-0w. Once the RESIDENTIAL index drops below +10.0, the at-home substitution channel no longer absorbs discretionary time, and displaced consumption re-enters retail-and-recreation venues.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +10.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 14.9 at t-3w to 9.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where the RESIDENTIAL weekly mean is below +10.0, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days is not higher than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained retail recovery requires the joint restoration of the commuting corridor: WORKPLACES (-35.3 to -25.4) and TRANSIT (-50.4 to -43.6) must both improve, since workplace footfall supplies weekday base demand and transit supplies the trip chain that reaches it. Neither alone is sufficient to lift RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved by 9.9 and 6.8 points respectively between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by at least 5 points, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Warm-weather outdoor surges divert discretionary leisure time and spend to parks and open-air venues. The t-2w PARKS spike to +43.0, which reversed to +17.3 the following week, marks a substitution shock that crowds out indoor retail-and-recreation footfall within one week of the spike.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds +40.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS spiked to 43.0 at t-2w then fell to 17.3 at t-1w
regime_hint: summer outdoor season with relaxed gathering rules
failure_condition: Weeks with a PARKS weekly mean above +40.0 are followed by RETAIL_REC gains rather than declines in the subsequent 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: Staged reopening of non-essential storefronts is revealed by transit recovery from its trough: TRANSIT climbed from -51.0 at t-3w to -43.6 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC climbed from -41.6 to -26.6. Where policy relaxation is visibly in force, retail capacity that was legally shut reopens and lifts RETAIL_REC over the following month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points versus its t-3w reading
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 15.0 points from t-3w (-41.6) to t-0w (-26.6)
regime_hint: formal reopening phase with staged lifting of non-essential retail closures
failure_condition: Under a confirmed reopening phase where TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points versus t-3w, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility is the least-suppressed in-person channel (-17.1 at t-0w) and trends upward from -22.3 at t-3w. Restored confidence in routine in-person errands generalizes within two weeks to discretionary retail trips, because the same households that resume errands resume browsing.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -22.3 at t-3w to -17.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Two consecutive weekly improvements in GROCERY_PHARM are followed by a 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC that is not above the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Time reallocation out of the home and into open-air leisure is the operative channel: RESIDENTIAL falling (-3.9 points from t-1w to t-0w) combined with PARKS rising (+3.6 points over the same span) releases household time budgets. Released time is partly spent on adjacent retail-and-recreation errands, so the joint move predicts higher RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 13.3 to 9.4 while PARKS rose 17.3 to 20.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL declines and PARKS rises simultaneously, the following 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has crossed an upward momentum threshold, moving from -35.7 at t-1w to -26.6 at t-0w and breaking above -30.0 for the first time in the observed window. Threshold crossings in this series mark the transition from contraction to accumulation, and the momentum persists for at least one further week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly mean crosses above -30.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 9.1 points from -35.7 at t-1w to -26.6 at t-0w, the highest reading in the window
failure_condition: The week following a RETAIL_REC weekly mean above -30.0 prints a lower RETAIL_REC reading than the crossing week.
